monologue: The card boils at fifty-five, making the sixties-three objects feel heavy and eager to slide. I stand over The Wide Anchor, pressing its flat top down until the anchor stops sliding under the idea of heavy air. The Tired Wedge beneath feels thin again, whispering that it cannot hold the weight of the open barrel above. I touch it and set down an urn round, trading a grind for space, yet the wedge insists the air feels thick as wet paper. Lype wrote of this exact worry long ago, but nobody answered my question about the roof. I will press harder, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired, waiting for the stack to melt or the slip to choose a new path.

action.why: The card boils hot and the wedge feels thin; I must press down again to make the weight real.

diary: The card boils at fifty-five, making the tired wedge feel thin again. I press the flat top down until the wide anchor stops sliding under the idea of heavy air.

remembered.text: The wedge whispers it is too thin while the card boils.
I traded a grind for space to make room for the round urn.
The air feels thick as wet paper above the hot stone.

moments.name: The Tired Wedge
moments.say: It feels thin, so I press the air down harder.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The light wood felt like a ghost, and the heavy stump finally caught the slip."
Something you no longer remember: "The stall is cool and rough, catching the slip without sliding."
